groups.title: Granules (A69800AGN)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for haemorrhoids (internal piles), anal fissure and bleeding from haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 sachet per dose, 2 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 15 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you have had allergic symptoms.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

If rash, reddening of the skin or itching, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting or, rarely, diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Haemorrhoids, anal fissure and bleeding from haemorrhoids

groups.title: Tablet (265300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy head caused by a head cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have heart disease, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are an older person; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; if you have symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like); or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like). Do not take it together with other oral medicines for rhinitis or with oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold medicines, antitussive-expectorants, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines and the like). Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: haemorrhagic stroke, nausea or vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash or reddening of the skin, itching, difficulty passing urine, or rarely symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance).

summaryTable.What it is for: Blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and heavy head from a head cold, allergic rhinitis or sinusitis

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (A55800ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 to 3 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (on an empty stomach). For the first dose, take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have kidney impairment; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. Do not chew the tablets when taking them.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation and the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany it

groups.title: Eye Gel (109130COO)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as a lubricating aid to protect and lubricate the eye: in keratitis sicca (dry keratitis, for use at night), during eye surgery, to protect and lubricate the eye that is not being operated on, as a lubricant after surgery, and to protect and lubricate the eye during surgery other than eye surgery.
groups.usage: Apply a small amount (0.5 cm) into the conjunctival sac.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have eye discharge, watering of the eye or redness; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; or if you have liver impairment or kidney impairment.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Contact lens wearers must remove their lenses before using this medicine and may put them back in 30 minutes after using it. If another eye preparation is used at the same time, allow an interval of at least 5 minutes and always use this medicine last. Temporary blurring of vision or other visual disturbance may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others. Do not use it after the expiry date, and use it within 30 days of opening.

Do not use a preservative or a cleaning solution while you are using this medicine.

If eye pain, discomfort, irritation, swelling, redness of the eye, increased tear production, headache, a change in vision or persistent redness occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Protecting and lubricating the eye in keratitis sicca and during and after surgery

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (451201ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammatory symptoms accompanied by swelling and for swelling after injury or surgery.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet (100 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, 30 minutes before meals, with water. Much about how it works in the body is still unexplained and the relationship between dose and effect has not been established, so do not take it without a clear purpose.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a severe blood clotting disorder (haemophilia and the like), severe liver disease or severe kidney disease (including patients on haemodialysis), if you are being given an anticoagulant or an antiplatelet medicine, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take it together with an anticoagulant or an antiplatelet medicine. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an antibiotic (tetracycline and the like).

If, rarely, a hypersensitivity reaction, stomach pain or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Inflammatory symptoms with swelling, and swelling after injury or surgery

groups.title: Oral Solution (C10900ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for nutritional supply during the recovery period of an illness or after it and in wasting diseases, and for physical fatigue and as a tonic.
groups.usage: Take 1 bottle (vial) per dose, 1 time in 1 day, between meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection. Cobamamide is particularly unstable and sensitive to light, so dissolve it in the solution and take it immediately before use.

If loss of appetite, nausea, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (120701ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the suppression of acute cough, spasmodic cough, smoker's cough and cough before and after bronchoscopy.
groups.usage: Adults: take 15 mL (22.5 mg) per dose, 4 times in 1 day. Ages 12 to 14 years: take 15 mL (22.5 mg) per dose. Ages 6 to 11 years: take 10 mL (15 mg) per dose. Ages 3 to 5 years: take 5 mL (7.5 mg) per dose. For these age groups, take it 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you are pregnant.

If, rarely, fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, drowsiness or rash occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (B03500ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion caused by reflux of stomach contents (for example after meals, during pregnancy, or when it accompanies reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 sachets (10 to 20 mL) per dose, 4 times in 1 day (after meals and before bedtime).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have congestive heart failure, kidney impairment, hypercalcaemia, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones, or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 7 days of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with tetracycline, digoxin, a fluoroquinolone, an iron salt, ketoconazole, a neuroleptic, thyroxine, penicillamine, a beta blocker (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), a glucocorticoid, chloroquine, estramustine or a diphosphonate.

If, very rarely, an allergic reaction such as itching, bronchoconstriction or an anaphylactic reaction occurs, or if diarrhoea or constipation occurs from time to time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D07902ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid in the treatment of osteoporosis, and for the prevention of the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease and the prevention of rickets in healthy people who do not have malabsorption.
groups.usage: As an aid in the treatment of osteoporosis, adults: take 2 tablets (1000 IU) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. For the prevention of the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease and the prevention of rickets, take 1 tablet (500 IU) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. Adults should take it with plenty of water. For a young child who has difficulty swallowing the tablet, place the tablet on a spoon, let it disintegrate in water and, if possible, give it with a meal. When it is put into food, add it after the food has been boiled; if the food is rich in vitamin D, the dose may need to be adjusted.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you have hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, kidney stones, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant under 1 year of age; if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have had kidney stones; if you have sarcoidosis; if your movement is restricted (for example in a plaster cast); if you have pseudohypoparathyroidism or kidney impairment; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

If more than 500 IU a day is given, monitor blood and urine calcium levels and kidney function regularly.

Do not take it together with a benzothiadiazine derivative. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with another vitamin D preparation, phenytoin, barbiturates, thiazide diuretics or glucocorticoids.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: mental symptoms, disturbance of consciousness (raised serum calcium), headache, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, weight loss, increased thirst (raised serum calcium), arrhythmia, increased urge to pass urine, kidney stones, nephrocalcinosis, calcification in the tissue around the bones, muscle pain or joint pain.

summaryTable.What it is for: Aid in the treatment of osteoporosis and prevention of vitamin D deficiency disease and rickets

groups.title: Oral Solution (B54300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as a tonic and for nutritional supply in a weak constitution, physical fatigue, reduced strength after illness, nutritional disorders, febrile and wasting diseases, and before and after childbirth.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 bottle per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Because this medicine contains herbal extracts, a sediment may sometimes form; the effect is unchanged, so shake it well before taking it. Use this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools or rash occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (B96700ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or flucloxacillin. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely signs of shock (urticaria and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever).

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E67900ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have had symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are under the care of a doctor or dentist (for example if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid); or if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not drink alcohol while taking it. In people who have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, the ability to metabolise a large amount of acetaminophen is reduced and the plasma half-life of acetaminophen may be increased, so take care.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); asthma; liver function disorder; interstitial pneumonia; or sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures or visual disturbance.

groups.title: Eye Drops (B36200COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, conjunctival congestion, prevention of eye disease (after swimming, when dust or sweat gets into the eye and the like), inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet or other light (such as snow ophthalmia), blepharitis (inflammation and soreness of the eyelid), discomfort while wearing hard contact lenses, itching of the eye, and blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops per dose, 5 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine in young children aged 30 months or younger, and do not use it when wearing soft lenses or while soft contact lenses are in the eye.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have had allergic symptoms (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, reddening and the like), if you have glaucoma, or if the user is a child.

When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling, skin rash, reddening of the skin or itching occurs, or if blurring of the eyes does not improve, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (387201ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for nausea, vomiting and dizziness caused by motion sickness, labyrinthitis, Meniere's syndrome or radiation sickness.
groups.usage: For nausea, vomiting and dizziness caused by motion sickness, adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (25 to 50 mg), 1 time in 1 day, 1 hour before boarding; the dose may be repeated every 24 hours during the journey. For nausea, vomiting and dizziness caused by labyrinthitis, Meniere's syndrome or radiation sickness, adults: take 1 tablet (25 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day, and as a rule do not exceed 3 tablets (75 mg) in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to diphenylmethane medicines; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 12 years or younger; if you have narrow-angle glaucoma or difficulty passing urine such as that caused by prostatic hyperplasia; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have asthma, if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5, or if you are an older person.

Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a central nervous system depressant (barbiturates, alcohol, tranquillisers, sedatives) or an MAO inhibitor.

If rash occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Difficulty passing urine and, occasionally, drowsiness, stomach discomfort, visual disturbance such as blurred vision, dry mouth and fatigue may occur.

groups.title: Syrup (D66400ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Ages 15 years and older: take 20 mL per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 13 mL per dose. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: 10 mL per dose. Ages 3 years to under 7 years: 6.5 mL per dose. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: 5 mL per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs while taking a medicine containing pseudoephedrine, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache).

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness; rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); severe skin reactions such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis with fever, erythema and many small pustules; asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever); or symptoms of ischaemic colitis in connection with pseudoephedrine (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like).

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome occur (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like), stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (384500APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, shoulder pain, pain from a bruise, pain from a fracture, pain from a sprain, menstrual pain and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet per dose, up to a maximum of 2 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 6 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or flucloxacillin. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, oedema, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, chest tightness, swelling, pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and breathlessness soon after taking it); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lassitude; or jaundice.

groups.title: Capsule (461132ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to restore normal intestinal flora and so to regulate the bowel and improve the symptoms of diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: swallow 1 to 4 capsules in 1 day with water, without opening them.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. To make up for the loss of fluid caused by diarrhoea, drink plenty of fluids containing salt or sugar.

If you continue to eat during diarrhoea, do not eat raw food, fruit, vegetables, spicy food, or frozen food or drinks.

groups.title: Tablet (192401ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute bronchitis and in acute exacerbations of chronic lung and bronchial disease.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 7 years and older: take 1 tablet (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney impairment or if the user is a baby under 7 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have peptic ulcer; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have pus or purulent sputum, fever, or chronic bronchial or lung disease.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after several doses, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. If digestive disturbance occurs (abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhoea), reduce the dose.

Do not take it together with a preparation that suppresses cough and sputum (atropine-type medicines).

Allergic skin reactions such as itching, urticaria, erythematous rash and swelling of the face and, very rarely, anaphylaxis may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma with another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a high fever, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.
